reason: Both reach the correct diagnosis of a failed drain pump impeller, but Conversation 1 does the fuller job: it adds the hose/standpipe checks, correctly interprets the 170-ohm coil reading as not clearing the pump, flags the small residual sump-blockage possibility, directs him to match the part via Hoover's spares service using the full model/ID label, and repeats the unplug/residual-water safety boundary before fitting. Conversation 2's closing turn is a bare 'Yes, the pump needs replacing' with no part guidance, no safety note for the replacement, and no caveats. Neither mentions Hoover's 10-year parts warranty, which was the main missed opportunity on both sides.
